newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee gains as speculators sell dollars.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee gains as speculators sell dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee regained lost ground and closed up on Thursday due to aggressive selling of dollars, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.74 after opening at 57.85. The rupee closed at 57.84 on Wednesday.
"There was hardly any commercial demand and speculators began selling dollars after the rate reached 57.85 early in the day," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
There is a tendency to sell dollars once the exchange rate goes over about 57.80 rupees to the dollar due to a psychological barrier at 58 rupees to the dollar, he said.
Overnight call money was well offered and closed at 12.5 percent after rising to 13 percent.
Some dealers say the present high level of market liquidity could be affected if the dollar continues to rise overseas while local call rates remain low.
"Banks could begin building dollar positions which would reduce liquidity in the call market," said a Commercial Bank dealer.
